crates.name: sar-cdc
crates.purpose: Content-defined chunking (CDC) algorithm and data model for SAR Protocol v1.0 Milestone 9a; stored CDC metadata is authoritative for parsing, while FASTCDC boundary-regeneration interoperability remains implementation-defined where the spec is incomplete.
features: FASTCDC algorithm (deterministic, two-level gear-hash; local-profile because spec parameters/domain are incomplete)
CDC algorithm ID registry (LITERAL=0x00, RABIN=0x01 optional unsupported, FASTCDC=0x02, BUZHASH=0x03 optional unsupported, CUSTOM=0xF0-0xFF unsupported)
CdcChunk, CdcMetadata, CdcMapRecord, CdcMapHeader, CdcMap public data structures
CDC_MAP TLV v1 binary parse/write (16-byte header + 48-byte records; self-describing via Hash_Algorithm_ID; parseable without boundary regeneration)
Recipe Mode structural validation (32-byte hash array only; no portable boundary-regeneration verification claim)
CdcError enum with Malformed/Unsupported/ReservedValue/LimitExceeded variants

crates.name: sar-core
crates.purpose: Canonical SAR wire-format, status/error, limits, and low-level parse/write helper APIs.
features: Milestone 10a stateless forward-only stream parser/writer state model.
Milestone 11a LFH Metadata API Completeness: expanded EntryInput, expanded EntryMetadata, FieldPresence<T> presence model, EntryKind, all metadata structs, complete LFH metadata round-trip.

Milestone 11b Filesystem Metadata Encode/Decode: FieldPresence-typed path_presence/permissions_presence/owner_presence/timestamps_presence in EntryMetadata, symlink_target metadata, symlink payload UTF-8 validation, directory payload validation, IS_SYMLINK->HAS_SYMLINKS validation, strict UTF-8, path/name length validation, deterministic round-trip tests.

Milestone 11c: Crate-boundary cleanup — fragment semantic logic moved to sar-fragmentation, sparse semantic logic moved to sar-sparse, loss-tolerant policy helpers added to sar-loss-tolerant, partition deliberately deferred.

Milestone 11c-cp (corrective pass): sar_core::fragment module removed (was pure re-exports); semantic sparse re-exports removed from sar_core::sparse (SparseExtent kept as architectural re-export); sar-loss-tolerant integrated into sar-fragmentation; FragmentError::PayloadSizeMismatch and DuplicateIndex added (always fatal); zero-length sparse extents now rejected; write_sparse_map now returns Result<Vec<u8>, SarError> (fail-closed on 32-bit truncation); error conversion bridges updated.

Milestone 11d: archive API architecture split — high-level archive reader/writer and stream parser orchestration moved to sar-archive; sar-core now owns canonical wire/status/limits and low-level helpers.

items.name: ArchiveReader::read_all_logical_files
items.signature: pub fn ArchiveReader<R>::read_all_logical_files(&mut self, allow_lossy: bool) -> Result<Vec<LogicalFile>, SarError>
items.description: High-level bounded extraction: reads all entries, assembles fragment groups via reconstruct_fragments, applies sparse zero-fill via apply_sparse_reconstruction, and returns LogicalFile values. Resets the read cursor so it can be called even after prior next_entry calls. When allow_lossy is false (default), a missing fragment returns FragmentGap. When allow_lossy is true and LOSS_TOLERANT is set, degraded output is returned with LogicalFile::is_degraded = true. AEAD and format errors are never suppressed. Sparse Map on a non-zero fragment index returns InvalidMap immediately (never suppressed by allow_lossy). Sparse reconstruction uses LFH Uncompressed Size as the final logical file size; trailing holes are filled with 0x00. CRC32 is verified over fully reconstructed bytes (including holes) when PER_FILE_CRC is set; CrcMismatch is returned on failure. Empty Areas (Name Length == 0, IS_FRAGMENT == 0) are excluded from the returned list. EXPANSION-BOMB PROTECTION: a tiny stored payload combined with a huge Uncompressed Size and a sparse extent near the end (e.g. Uncompressed Size=1025, max_decoded_entry_size=1024, sparse map {offset=1024, length=1}, one stored byte) is rejected with SAR_ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED before any large allocation is attempted — not SAR_ERR_INVALID_MAP, because the sparse map is structurally valid. The same protection applies to fragmented sparse entries using fragment-0's Uncompressed Size.
items.ffi_notes: High-value FFI candidate; Vec<LogicalFile> ownership needs care.

items.name: apply_bsdiff
items.signature: pub fn apply_bsdiff(base: &[u8], patch: &[u8], expected_target_size: u64, limits: &BsdiffLimits) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PatchError>
items.description: Applies a SAR BSDIFF v1 patch (`SARBSD01`) to the supplied base bytes. Validates the 32-byte header (magic, block lengths, new file size), reads uncompressed Control/Diff/Extra blocks, applies control triples using sign-magnitude decoding, and returns the reconstructed target. Base reads beyond the end of base use 0x00. Caller supplies base explicitly; no lookup is performed.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Base object bytes supplied explicitly by the caller.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.description: SAR BSDIFF v1 patch payload bytes (`SARBSD01`).

parameters.name: expected_target_size
parameters.description: Expected reconstructed target size (must equal LFH Uncompressed Size); must match New_File_Size in the patch header.

parameters.name: limits
parameters.description: Resource limits for block sizes, control triple count, and output size.

errors: PatchError::PatchFailed for invalid magic, negative lengths, malformed or truncated control triples, block overread, trailing unused diff/extra bytes, seek-before-zero, output size mismatch
PatchError::BaseMissing when base is required but not supplied (checked by caller before this call)
items.ffi_notes: No C ABI in this milestone.

items.name: apply_vcdiff
items.signature: pub fn apply_vcdiff(base: &[u8], patch: &[u8], expected_target_size: u64, limits: &VcdiffLimits) -> Result<Vec<u8>, PatchError>
items.description: Applies a VCDIFF (RFC 3284) patch to the supplied base bytes. Validates the 4-byte magic header, decodes windows and instruction tables, and reconstructs the target output. Supports VCD_SOURCE and VCD_TARGET address spaces; ADD, COPY, and RUN instructions; default code table. Caller supplies base explicitly; no lookup is performed.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Base object bytes supplied explicitly by the caller.

parameters.name: expected_target_size
parameters.description: Expected reconstructed target size (must equal LFH Uncompressed Size).

parameters.name: limits
parameters.description: Resource limits for window count, instruction count, and output size.

errors: PatchError::PatchFailed for invalid header, malformed varints, invalid instructions, copy out of range, output size mismatch, truncated stream
PatchError::Unsupported for unsupported VCDIFF secondary compression flags/compressors
PatchError::BaseMissing when base is required but not supplied (checked by caller before this call)
items.ffi_notes: No C ABI in this milestone.

crates.name: sar-stream
crates.purpose: In-memory Stateful Streaming Mode session layer over sar-core structural parsing.
features: Activation requires NO_INDEX + non-zero Stream ID + valid SESSION_INIT.
Session UUID binding, per-stream sequence continuity/wraparound, and SESSION_* frame parsing/writing.
Filesystem/session OP_CODE namespace validation with in-memory event/action output only.
LOSS_TOLERANT can surface authenticated degraded output as SAR_WARN_INCOMPLETE but does not suppress auth, decompression, patch, or structural failures.
No transport framing, networking, sockets, or async runtime.

errors: Returns SarError::StreamState for invalid activation, duplicate Stream IDs, or sequence discontinuities.
Returns SarError::LimitExceeded / TooManyStreams when configured ResourceLimits are exceeded.
safety_notes: Requires NO_INDEX + non-zero Stream ID + valid SESSION_INIT before stateful mode becomes active.
No network I/O, transport framing, or real filesystem mutation is performed.
items.ffi_notes: Possible future opaque-handle wrapper because the API is already transport-free and in-memory.

crates.name: sar-transport
crates.purpose: Transport abstraction traits, deterministic in-memory TCP-like/QUIC-like harness over sar-stream, SAR-over-TCP binding (M10d), and SAR-over-QUIC binding (M10e, quic feature).
features: Transport abstraction surface: TransportBindingKind, TransportConfig, TransportStreamId, TransportStreamState, TransportAction, SarTransportBinding.
Deterministic in-memory harness with TCP-like non-interleaved policy and QUIC-like concurrent-stream policy.
Active SAR Stream ID uniqueness, duplicate/limit rejection, rejected-ID unbound invariant, and SESSION_CLOSE unbind/reuse behavior.
Status/ACK hooks mapped from sar-stream events/actions using SessionStatusFrame and SessionAckFrame types.
Explicit-time heartbeat/watchdog hooks with no background timers/tasks or real network I/O.
M10d TCP binding: TcpSarConnection<S> wraps any Read+Write stream and drives M10c TCP policy over real bytes (std::net, no async, no TLS, no QUIC).
M10d TCP binding enforces bounded read_buffer_size and write_buffer_size limits before any allocation.
M10d TCP binding serializes SESSION_STATUS/SESSION_ACK outbound frames when bidirectional control is active.
M10e QUIC binding (quic feature): QuicSarListener, QuicSarConnection, QuicSarStream, connect_quic using quinn 0.11 + rustls 0.23 + tokio 1.
M10e: explicit QuicServerIdentity (DER cert chain + DER private key) and QuicClientTrust (CustomCaDer or InsecureSkipVerifyForTestsOnly).
M10e: active SAR Stream ID uniqueness per QUIC connection; duplicate SESSION_INIT fails closed with SAR_ERR_STREAM_STATE.
M10h: additional QUIC control streams begin directly with LFH-encoded SESSION_CONTROL and associate by QUIC connection + LFH Stream ID.
M10e: same bidirectional QUIC stream supports reverse SESSION_ACK/SESSION_STATUS when CAP_BIDIRECTIONAL_CONTROL is active.
M10e: KMS Mode 0x04 TLS_EXPORTER supported for QUIC connections; export_keying_material derives keying material via quinn TLS exporter API.
M10e: all connection/stream limits enforced before allocation.

resource_limits.model: unified ResourceLimits struct threaded through all parsing and reconstruction paths
resource_limits.primary_protection: Configured ResourceLimits are the primary and deterministic protection against allocation-based DoS. There is no separate runtime memory budget by design.
resource_limits.defense_in_depth_note: Runtime memory tracking is not implemented. Configured limits are both the primary and only protection layer; they are not defense-in-depth.
resource_limits.allocation_gate: ResourceLimits::allocation_len is the single gate for all u64-to-usize conversions. No conversion bypasses it.
resource_limits.limit_exceeded_error: SAR_ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (SarError::LimitExceeded) is returned before any dangerous allocation.

sparse_expansion_bomb.attack_shape: tiny stored payload + huge Uncompressed Size + sparse extent near end of logical file
sparse_expansion_bomb.protection: apply_sparse_reconstruction and read_all_logical_files reject oversized logical_size before allocation. Error is LimitExceeded, not InvalidMap.
sparse_expansion_bomb.fragmented_sparse: Fragmented sparse entries use fragment-0's Uncompressed Size; the same LimitExceeded check applies.
sparse_expansion_bomb.test: pipeline_memory_tests::sparse_expansion_bomb_reject and sparse_expansion_bomb_bounded_success verify reject and bounded-success paths

compression_expansion.protection: sar-compression enforces a caller-provided max_output_size parameter. Decompression output is bounded by max_decoded_entry_size.

fec_recovery_working_set.fec_internal_ceiling: sar-fec caps XOR and Reed-Solomon parity allocations at 256 MiB internal ceiling.

cli_resource_safety.extract: Validates sparse apparent size against max_decoded_entry_size; creates temp file; scatter-gather seeks; renames only on success. Does not allocate large zero buffers for sparse holes.
cli_resource_safety.repair: Pre-checks archive size before fs::read; enforces max_repair_working_set; does not finalize output after limit failure.
cli_resource_safety.error_reporting: CLI resource-limit failures reported as: resource-limit error (SAR_ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED)

loss_tolerant.note: allow_lossy never bypasses ResourceLimits. Fragment gaps filled with zeros are bounded by max_loss_tolerant_gap.
loss_tolerant.aead_note: AEAD authentication failures are never suppressed by allow_lossy or LOSS_TOLERANT flag.

aead.note: AEAD decryption failures are never suppressed. Plaintext is not released until authentication succeeds. Working buffer is zeroized on failure before error return.

arbitrary_byte_erasure_repair.reason: spec gap — no normative byte-to-block mapping defined for arbitrary byte erasure positions
arbitrary_byte_erasure_repair.behavior: plan_archive_repair returns RecoveryUnavailable for non-block-aligned erasures

cdc.external_provider_handling: CDC_EXT_PROVIDER is parsed as inert metadata only; no network/provider access is performed in M9a.
cdc.recipe_hash_verification: Unavailable as a portable claim while recipe hash algorithm/profile is not fully specified.
cdc.boundary_regeneration_verification: Unavailable as a portable claim until FastCDC parameters and CDC transformation domain are normatively specified or encoded.
cdc.cdc_map_interpretation: CDC_MAP is treated as stored metadata for parsing/structural validation; it is not proof of portable cross-writer deterministic chunking.
cdc.metadata_authority: For M9a, stored CDC map/catalog metadata is authoritative for parsing and interpretation when self-consistent.
